And in this year, Sultan Mas'ud sent to Caliph Rashid,
and demanded of him three hundred thousand dinars that al-Mustarshid his father had promised him while he was with him;
and three hundred thousand dinars more, saying, "Collect aid for me from the people of Baghdad,
and also send me the customary dues of the new caliphate, as is the custom."
The Caliph, however, gathered his nobles and took counsel with them
as to what he should answer.
And they advised:
that he should gather troops and encounter Mas'ud (in {OCR?} the Turks).
And he accepted their counsel,
and opened his treasures,
and brought out much gold,
and enlisted numerous troops.
And he sent to the envoy of Mas'ud and said to him:
"As for the gold which my father promised,
it was for the sake of his deliverance from you,
yet you killed him;
and I am going to avenge him from you.
And you have nothing from me except the sword."
When the envoy heard these things,
he left and fled.
And the Caliph began to take care diligently for the construction of the wall (walls) and ramparts.
And in those days Zangi, the lord of Mosul, arrived to the aid of the Caliph;
and Da'ud, the nephew of Sultan Mas'ud, also arrived.
And the Caliph wished to abolish the proclamation of Mas'ud
and to proclaim Da'ud.
Zangi, however, was not willing, and said:
"Do not provoke Mas'ud too much,
and reply to this youth:
'Go, confront your uncle;
if you are victorious and established,
we will proclaim you.'"
The Caliph, however, did not accept,
but abolished the name of Mas'ud,
and proclaimed Da'ud sultan.
Mas'ud, then, sent to the Caliph and said to him:
"We have no further need of you,
and behold, we have appointed as caliph one who is worthy from the lineage of Ali {OCR? - or Abbas?}.
As for you, look for yourself another place,
and go out and depart wherever you wish."
Then the Caliph was shaken,
and sent to Bihruz, the emir of Tikrit,
and asked of him that he might go to him and fortify himself in the fortress of Tikrit.
Bihruz, however, answered:
"I am a servant of Mas'ud,
and if he demands you from me,
I cannot withhold you from him."
Then he was compelled,
the Caliph, to prepare for war with Mas'ud;
and he pitched his tents outside Baghdad,
and with him was Zangi and the rest of the nobles.
